articles.title: Parliament clears stricter anti-paper leak Bill with harsher penalties, fast-track courts
articles.summary: Parliament has approved amendments to India's anti-paper leak law, significantly tightening penalties for examination fraud and expanding enforcement powers. The revised legislation introduces special fast-track courts, empowers the Centre to set up a dedicated investigation task force, and broadens the scope of offences covered. The government says the changes aim to protect the integrity of public examinations and restore confidence among millions of students appearing for competitive tests.

articles.title: Dabur shares drop 3% after FSSAI bars FMCG major from selling products with '100%' guarantee claims
articles.summary: Dabur India shares fell nearly 3% after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) barred the FMCG company from selling certain food products carrying misleading "100%" claims. The regulator said labels such as "100% Natural" and "100% Pure" violate the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018, as they are ambiguous, unverifiable and likely to mislead consumers.

articles.title: Collegium for consistency
articles.summary: The article calls for the Supreme Court collegium to establish consistent norms regarding transparency, legitimate confidentiality, and the recording of reasons for judicial appointments and decisions. This is important for ensuring accountability and uniformity in the collegium system, which appoints judges to higher courts in India.

articles.title: Neurodiversity & the future of work
articles.summary: Jaishankar Natarajan, CEO and director of the India Autism Centre (IAC), highlights the importance of neurodiversity in the future of work. The article emphasizes the need for inclusive employment policies and workplace adaptations to support neurodivergent individuals. It underscores the broader societal and economic benefits of integrating neurodiverse talent into the workforce.

articles.title: The E20 debate is asking the wrong question
articles.summary: The article, authored by Maulik Shah, founder of Aditya Engimach, critiques the ongoing debate around E20 fuel (20% ethanol-blended petrol) in India. It argues that the discussion is focusing on the wrong questions regarding ethanol adoption, which has implications for India's energy policy and climate goals. The piece highlights the need for a more informed policy approach to ethanol blending in the transportation sector.
articles.raw_summary: This article is authored by Maulik Shah, founder and managing director, Aditya Engimach.

articles.title: Should social media platforms be held accountable for what users post?
articles.summary: Parliament is reviewing whether social media platforms should be legally accountable for illegal content posted by users. Experts are divided on whether existing rules adequately address online safety without infringing on free speech. The debate centers on finding the right balance between holding platforms responsible and protecting users' rights.
articles.raw_summary: As Parliament examines social media accountability, experts are divided over whether platforms should be held legally responsible for illegal posts by users or whether existing rules strike the right balance between online safety and free speech.
